method:
Graphical abstract for a journal paper. The figure should tell a single visual story, read left to right:

1. INPUT (left): A single 2D indoor image (photograph or architectural floor plan) enters the pipeline.

2. VLM ABSTRACTION (center-left): A Vision-Language Model (Gemini) processes the image and extracts a structured 3D scene description (JSON) containing room geometry, obstacles, and ventilation openings. Show this as a transformation from flat image to a simple 3D wireframe/block representation.

3. AUTOMATED CFD (center-right): The 3D scene is automatically meshed (tetrahedral mesh) and solved with OpenFOAM to produce a steady-state CFD solution. Show a velocity contour or streamline visualization inside the 3D room.

4. OUTPUT (right): The final CFD result with key performance numbers: Structural similarity 0.781, CFD agreement 0.477, evaluated on 100 benchmark cases.

Overall message: 'From a single image to CFD in minutes, no manual geometry modelling required.'

Style: Clean academic graphical abstract suitable for Elsevier journal. Minimal text, strong visual flow left-to-right with arrows. Color scheme: professional blues and whites. No excessive decoration. The figure should be self-explanatory at a glance.

Aspect ratio: approximately 2.5:1 (wide horizontal, matching Elsevier graphical abstract spec of ~531x1328 px minimum).
caption: Graphical abstract: A single 2D image of an indoor space is processed by a vision-language model to extract a 3D scene description, which is automatically meshed and solved with OpenFOAM. The framework achieves a mean structural score of 0.781 and CFD agreement of 0.477 across 100 benchmark cases.
